title: The Rise And Fall Of Liberal Democracy’s Shared Fiction | NOEMA
gist: Macario Schettino argues that societies cohere around 'transcendent beliefs' that were historically disrupted by climate shocks but, since the printing press in 1517, are disrupted by communications technology — and that the postwar citizenship framework broke publicly at the Munich Security Conference on Feb. 14, 2025. His load-bearing claim is that every prior communications disruption was eventually tamed by the mature form of the same technology, so the social-media crisis will be resolved through AI-shaped platforms rather than by retreating from them.

insights.claim: Large-scale human cooperation depends on 'transcendent beliefs' — faith in something that outlasts individual death — and when those beliefs break down, the political order built on them breaks down with them.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Treat legitimacy crises as belief-system failures rather than policy failures — policy fixes will not restore institutional trust if the underlying fiction has collapsed.

insights.claim: For most of human history, belief-system transitions were triggered by climate shocks — the end of the last Ice Age producing ancestor worship, the 8.2-ka event producing polytheistic small gods that integrated clans into early cities, and the 4.2-ka event producing moralizing Big Gods that legitimated territorial states and empires.

insights.so_what: This makes media-platform transitions, not economic cycles, the leading indicator for regime-level political instability.

insights.claim: The crisis of liberal democracy was laid bare on Feb. 14, 2025, when JD Vance told European leaders at the Munich Security Conference that the gravest threat to their continent came from within — governments distrusting their own people, courts overturning elections and the retreat of free speech.

insights.so_what: Dating the rupture to a specific speech gives a concrete marker for when transatlantic security and trade assumptions stopped being safe to underwrite.

insights.so_what: Global trade volumes rest on a shared fiction rather than on enforceable structure; erosion of the fiction degrades the trade system before any treaty formally changes.

insights.claim: The printing press produced the first communications-driven belief change and simultaneously pushed the transcendent frame from collectivity toward individuality, since Luther's claim that anyone could read the Bible without priestly intermediation let individualist strains flourish in Northern Europe.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: New media do not just change who speaks — they systematically shift the locus of legitimacy toward the individual, which is the pattern to expect from AI-mediated platforms too.

insights.claim: Communications disruptions carry extreme human costs: the religious tensions unleashed by printed Lutheran ideas laid the foundations for the Thirty Years' War, in which roughly a third of Central Europe's population died.

insights.so_what: The historical base rate for media-driven transitions includes catastrophic conflict, which argues against complacency about the current phase.

insights.claim: The Lisbon earthquake of 1755, striking a major European capital on All Saints' Day, became a public test of which transcendent frame would hold — divine punishment versus natural disaster — and the Enlightenment emerged as the answer, producing the American and French revolutions.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Catastrophes act as public tests that resolve competing worldviews quickly; watch for a comparable stress event to force resolution of today's frame contest.

insights.claim: Mass media made it possible for one voice to reach millions, which produced totalitarianism's specific signature — the manufactured national emotion — running from 'The Birth of a Nation' in 1915 through the radio discourses of Mussolini and Hitler and Riefenstahl's and Eisenstein's films.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Media architecture determines the shape of the political pathology it enables — concentration produces manufactured unity, fragmentation produces something else entirely.

insights.claim: Postwar liberal democracy was structurally a television system: one person on a screen could reach millions with a handful of simple ideas — employment, wages, taxes, the security state — which parties packaged as platforms and sold at elections.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Party platforms are an artifact of broadcast economics; as broadcast dies, the platform-and-election product itself becomes obsolete regardless of party ideology.

insights.claim: The postwar system began dissolving in 2006 with modern social media platforms, accelerated in 2007 with the smartphone and ruptured between 2008 and 2011 with the Great Recession, because simple national ideas could no longer hold attention against a feed of identity, grievance, conspiracy and culture war.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO

insights.claim: The citizenship framework has been brittle from the start because it is the hardest transcendent frame humans have tried to inhabit — it offers no comfort, asking strangers to accept that what unites them is primarily a balance of market prices and votes.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: A worldview that provides no consolation carries permanent defection risk, which explains the recurring, structural nature of populist revolt rather than treating it as episodic.

insights.claim: Contemporary right-wing populism — MAGA in its developed forms, Orbán in Hungary, Le Pen in France — is structurally identical to the ancien régime's resistance to the French Revolution and to 19th-century Spanish Carlism: an attempt to bring back the god of the tribe.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: If populism is a restorationist reflex rather than a novel program, it will persistently win elections yet fail to construct durable institutions — expect volatility, not a new stable order.

insights.claim: The progressive identitarian project that spread through Western universities and institutions over the last decade is a descendant of the same utopian impulse as Jacobinism and Marxism-Leninism, sharing a sacred theory of history, an enlightened vanguard, an institutional remaking project and a moral charge against dissenters.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Framing both political poles as anachronistic descendants of 19th-century movements predicts that neither can stabilize governance — a structurally bearish view on institutional predictability.

insights.claim: In the 20th century restorationism and utopianism fought each other for control of states; in the 21st they fight for control of cultures inside states, so the conflict is no longer over the means of production but over the production of meaning.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Cultural-institutional capture, not electoral or economic outcomes, is where the real contest resolves — watch media, universities and platforms rather than legislatures.

themes.theme: The taming pattern and the AI wager

insights.claim: Every previous communications disruption was eventually tamed by the mature form of the same technology that caused it — the press that broke Christendom produced the Enlightenment, the revolutionary newspaper matured into the stable citizen-democracy's daily companion, and propaganda radio and film gave way to regulated broadcast journalism.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: The historical pattern argues against regulatory strategies that suppress the disruptive medium and for those that accelerate its mature institutional forms.
insights.quote: In each case, what initially fragmented the public sphere is what, in its maturer form, eventually rebuilt it.

insights.claim: The social-media disruption will not be resolved by abandoning social media but by its next iteration as shaped by artificial intelligence, with AI simultaneously the most likely amplifier of current chaos and the most plausible candidate to tame it.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: A structurally bullish case for AI-mediated information platforms as the successor infrastructure to social feeds — the incumbent feed model is the thing being replaced.
insights.quote: The new transcendent framework, whatever its content, will not arrive in spite of these technologies. It will arrive through them.

insights.so_what: Platform ownership and governance become the contested political asset of the next era, the way broadcast licenses were in the last.

insights.claim: These transitions take generations to settle: the Reformation required 131 years to reach the Peace of Westphalia, the Enlightenment took longer, and the mass-media transition produced two world wars and a Cold War before the postwar order stabilized — making the social-media transition still very young.

insights.claim: Institutions still function but with declining legitimacy because they were designed for citizens organized by broadcast, populists rise but cannot build because their proposals cannot scale to encompass the full society, and intellectuals diagnose but cannot resolve the crisis.

insights.claim: The new transcendent fiction will most likely be assembled by the next generation, who grow up inside the new technologies and will accept as self-evident the conditions that current adults find frustrating or untenable.
insights.speaker: MACARIO SCHETTINO
insights.so_what: Generational turnover, not persuasion or policy, is the mechanism of resolution — a multi-decade timeline that current political actors cannot shortcut.
